transformation.title: A location being turned into an integrated farm
transformation.lede: The strategic intent is to transform a difficult-looking site — described in review as dump-yard-like — into a working integrated farm, after moving the work to the side with better access. Before-photographs and the exact plot identity are pending confirmation. Do not read the stages below as a finished documentary.
transformation.pending: This sequence is the intended story. Before-photographs, the named plot, and completion status are not yet approved — the frames are empty on purpose.

stages.title: What is being developed
stages.body: The vision is a live integrated farm — crop, water, animals and market on one holding — not a painted backdrop.

stages.title: The emerging model
stages.body: Leftover becomes input: pond, bund horticulture, livestock, bio-inputs and careful tools. That is the farm people should be able to walk.

stages.title: The larger aim
stages.body: The mobilisation already on this project is about 5,000 village integrated farms, with one NRB patron each. That is a goal, not a result already achieved.

sections.title: Decision-makers and the public gathering, in one living week.
sections.body: A conference gathers buyers in a hall. A typical mass event gathers a crowd without the people who decide budgets. Durga Puja in Bengal is when the city is outdoors together. Bharatiya Krishak Samaj Pujo places an agricultural story — farmer, award, live farm — inside that week. That is the intended setting. It is not a guaranteed footfall, media-reach, or income figure.

sections.title: Season 1 of a three-year movement.
sections.body: Joining the first season means being present at the start of a platform that is meant to continue: a continuing narrative, a visible transformation of a place into an integrated farm, and ongoing participation across three years. Year 2 and Year 3 programmes are not published here. This is a seasonal storytelling model — not a claim that the Puja is a television reality show.

sections.title: Facts already on this project — not new statistics.
sections.body: Sharadiya 2026 is dated 16–20 October 2026 in Kolkata, West Bengal; the exact pandal address is still to be announced. The gathering is organised as Bharatiya Krishak Samaj Pujo. The mobilisation described on this project is a target of about 5,000 village farms and about 5,000 NRB patrons, with ₹1 lakh as the proposed seed figure per farm. Those figures are a goal. This page does not invent footfall, media-reach, or income numbers.

farmers.h1: A farming livelihood you can walk — not a slogan on a pandal wall.
farmers.lede: This Pujo puts the annadata in view, honours farmers who are rarely photographed, and then shows Integrated Farming as a working system on small land. The live demonstration is being built. How you formally join a farm programme is not a fake registration on this page.

sections.title: One crop carries the whole year’s risk. A loop does not.
sections.body: On a small holding, a single standing crop — often paddy — meets weather, price and bought inputs at once. An integrated farm keeps several enterprises on the same land so leftover becomes the next input: pond silt to beds, residue to animals, manure to soil and energy. That is the livelihood this Pujo is trying to show, in plain view.

sections.title: The annadata is the person who feeds the household.
sections.body: The Puja is when Bengal gathers. This gathering is meant to bring the unnamed farmer into recognition — including an award ceremony on Ashtami evening for farmers the state does not usually photograph. Nominations on the main site have no entry fee. Recognition is not a substitute for a working farm. It is why the farm story is allowed to stand next to the festival.

sections.title: Pond, bund, animals, soil, and careful tools.
sections.body: The model already written for this project is a closed loop on about 1 to 2.5 acres: a pond as water and fish; bund horticulture in tiers; livestock and poultry beside the water; on-farm compost and bio-inputs; then monitoring tools where they earn their keep. It is a working sketch, not a guarantee of anyone’s income.

sections.title: A live farm is being built in the East Kolkata Wetlands, 500 metres from Sector V.
sections.body: That location is already on this project as the 2026 pavilion — a working farm, not only a festive facade. Status: being built. Whether the dump-yard-like transformation story and this wetland plot are the same piece of land is pending confirmation. Daily dispatches will appear when they are posted.

stakeholders.lede: This briefing is for government stakeholders, institutions, influencers and ecosystem partners. It explains the initiative and how to request a conversation. West Bengal’s assembly has 294 seats; that number is the scale of the stakeholder universe, not a list of endorsements. Nothing here is a claimed government partnership or scheme.

sections.title: A seasonal Puja that carries a live farming demonstration and a longer mobilisation.
sections.body: Bharatiya Krishak Samaj Pujo is a Sharadiya 2026 gathering in Kolkata under Bharatiya Krishak Samaj as organizing partner, organised with KarmYog for the 21st Century. Beside the festival sits a live integrated-farm demonstration (East Kolkata Wetlands, 500 metres from Sector V, being built) and a stated aim to seed about 5,000 village farms.

sections.title: Farming is the thing the festival was timed to — and the thing public life often skips.
sections.body: West Bengal’s small and marginal holdings, input costs, flood and cyclone risk, and seasonal cash gaps are already described in this project’s Integrated Farming material. This page does not add new impact percentages. It asks institutional readers to look at a public demonstration they can eventually walk, and a mobilisation that needs local legitimacy.

sections.title: Festival as the visible week; farm as the continuing work.
sections.body: The Puja is the public platform — neighbourhood, awards, exhibition. The farm is the proof. The 5,000-farm aim pairs each village site with a patron and a local farmer team. Payment is not taken on this website. Venue and committee remain to be announced where they are not yet named.

sections.title: A closed-loop holding, shown in public.
sections.body: The model on file combines water, horticulture, livestock, soil repair and careful tools on one small farm. The demonstration is being built so the model is not only a diagram in a brief.

sections.title: About 5,000 village farms — a mobilisation already on this project.
sections.body: Those numbers are a goal, not a completed census and not a government target adopted by any department on this page. Patronage amounts live on the NRB door. This briefing does not sell a commercial package.

sections.title: Institutions can look, question, and help the work sit in the right places.
sections.body: MLAs, officers and civic voices are invited to understand the execution, visit when the demonstration can be walked, and say clearly what would make the village-farm pairing responsible. This is a request for a briefing, not a campaign advertisement.
